catalog_quote: Stress occurs basically on the last syllable of Karo words. Less frequently, it occurs on penultimate syllables. These occurrences are predictable in terms of segmental and suprasegmental factors. ... From the segmental point of view, stress can be predicted by the onset of the last syllable: if it is a voiced stop consonant, /b/, /r/ or /g/, then the stress shifts one syllable to the left. /yaba/ ['yaba] 'rodent (sp.)' ... /aoro/ [a'oro] 'parrot' ... /macirup/ [ma'c:irup] 'bird (sp.)' ... If the onset of the last syllable is of any other kind rather than /b/, /r/ or /g/ then the stress falls on the last syllable. /peon/ [pe'odn] 'skin' ... /kuru?cu/ [kuru?'cu] 'saliva' ... /kiriwep/ [kiri'wep] 'butterfly' ... audit.reasoning: The deciding quotation is verbatim in the held 1999 UCSB reference grammar at the stated locator (sec. 2.5, printed pp. 30-34, PDF pp. 46-50). That grammar is the fullest and latest description of Karo and every Glottolog descriptive reference is by the same author; the earlier phonology monograph (1989 MA, fetched sources now to gives the identical analysis as an ordered rule hierarchy (high tone > nasal vowel > penult if final onset /b r g/ > final), so the 'segmental' (onset-conditioned, right-edge, with tone/nasality override and a listed set of lexical exceptions) coding stands. No instrumental study located

sources.quote: 'A ocorrência do acento no Karo é previsível, sendo condicionada por três fatores fonológicos distintos: a) pelo tom; b) pela nasalidade; c) pela qualidade do fonema que inicia a última sílaba das palavras. ... regras estabelecidas em ordem hierárquica: 1) São acentuadas todas as sílabas com tom alto (/mόa/ ['mbόa] jabuti); 2) Se não há tom alto, acentua-se a sílaba com vogal nasal (/wakãya/ [wa'k:ãya] cutia); 3) Se não há tom alto nem vogal nasal, acentua-se a penúltima sílaba se esta preceder /b/, /r/ ou /g/ (/yaba/ ['yaba] paca, /aoro/ [a'oro] papagaio); 4) Nos demais casos é acentuada a úl
